reviews.text:
We contacted this clinic following a recommendation from a new veterinary practice we'd visited for a second consultation, because at the time we were being treated by another well-known clinic in Milan, where we were not only wasting time but also (a lot!) of money with constant tests, without ever managing to obtain a cure.
We fortunately ended up at the San Francesco Clinic, asking for an internist, and with Dr. Luperto, we were finally treated properly: after a small battery of blood tests and diagnostic tests, our cat was immediately diagnosed with a strong suspicion of FIP, and without wasting time, we immediately began treatment, which to date, almost three months later, has practically cured our cat.
Our problem was handled with absolute professionalism and transparency: every necessary test was carefully evaluated, but above all, it was offered to us and promptly quoted, unlike other places where owners are assumed to have unlimited financial resources.
We can highly recommend San Francesco, a competent but above all honest veterinary center.
Thank you for saving our Cesare... from a lethargic cat, extremely thin and constantly feverish, probably with only a few months to live, we now have a real feline at home. 😇

Incompetent storytellers. I took my cat to the hospital for a lump in her throat. They performed various ultrasounds on everything except the lump (without even realizing it was a massive mass in her lung) and absolutely recommended a three-day hospital stay for further investigations at a modest cost of €2,000. I took the cat home and the next day took him to a reputable clinic where they performed all the necessary tests in one morning for less than a quarter of the cost. You decide. Also, the reception staff were really rude. They answered the phone while making impatient gestures towards the customers. I stayed there for three and a half hours, so I had the opportunity to overhear several phone calls.
Thank you so much for your review! We're happy you had a great experience. Kind regards,
I had two important tests done on my dog. The staff was perfect and very courteous. I highly recommend them.

I express my deepest appreciation not only for the qualified facility and the highly competent specialist care (as a doctor, I can say this without hesitation), but also for the attention to my dog's well-being during her hospital stay and for the empathy you showed me in a dramatic situation. A special thanks to Dr. Galizzi, a brilliant, attentive, and humane cardiologist... his help is priceless. I know that Diana dal Ponte also thanks you for everything you've done for her.
It's not true that the emergency room is always open: not on Saturdays and Sundays.

I brought my daughter Lucy to you for the first time. She's a cat who usually gets a real headache at the vet, but with Dr. Pansecchi, she was fantastic! The reception staff were also very quick and, above all, very kind.
Thank you so much, we had a great time. Lucy thanks you too!

I'm writing this after a few months. Recently, in early September, my cat passed away from a suspected five-centimeter pancreatic tumor (90% likely, as a kidney was also involved). I had an abdominal ultrasound at San Francesco on May 14th, which showed no signs of any abnormality, following a visit to San Francesco on May 4th. The visit was quite a nightmare: the room was crowded, the doctor completely lacking empathy, more focused on demonstrating his scientific knowledge (starting with taking a throat sample from the poor cat, whom I'd never seen in 14 years), and prescribing medications without explanation, with subsequent communications exclusively via email. I brought the cat, who already had extensive symptoms of the tumor that had subsequently developed, and the medication I was given only made them worse (which stopped when I stopped it). In August/September, due to travel constraints, I took the cat to two vets in two different locations and was able to test their expertise, empathy, and unstinting availability (among other things, a practice in one of the most expensive places in Italy, which, on the contrary, turned out to be "affordable"). Starting with the initial visit with an X-ray (which wasn't done on May 4th), which immediately revealed an abnormally enlarged thoracic lymph node.

Dear Antonella, thank you so much for your review. We appreciate you taking the time to share your experience!
Best regards from our entire team 🥰 …
A terrible clinic, there are some kids who don't understand anything about veterinary stuff. If I could, I would have given them 0 stars.

Aside from Dr. Ferriani, whom I respect, unfortunately, I can only say that there's considerable room for improvement, and regarding the clinical expertise of the various professionals and their communication with patients, this is based on my experience.
Furthermore, I find it excessive to charge €600 for the assisted cremation (which is performed in Piacenza) of a 6-kilo dog, a procedure I've had elsewhere...
It's a shame, it's no longer the Veterinary Clinic I knew and thanked so much in the past... Patrizia Salvini

Exceptional clinic.
It's rare to find such kind, helpful, and competent people.
Fantastic ❤️

I just called (August 18th, 2:18 PM) and was in a panic about a foal. I asked if they cared for horses, and then I asked if they had the number of an equine vet. The receptionist laughed and said no. It's nothing to laugh about if I tell you a foal is dying. Maybe you should change jobs... if animal suffering makes you laugh. Choose your staff a little better.

The doctor saved my cat's eye. With her care, it wasn't necessary to remove it.
Well done!
Really clean structure, super kind and competent staff
Thank you so much for your review, Violante! We're so happy you had such a positive experience. Best regards from our entire team!

Thanks again to Dr. Luperto and Dr. Biagini for doing everything possible to treat my cat Russell. They are incredibly professional, but also empathetic and helpful.
A cutting-edge facility.
Excellent clinic

A profound appreciation for the courtesy, competence, kindness, and ability to listen and understand, the punctuality in meeting and visiting appointments, and the clarity of the presentation that allows even the uninitiated to understand; the welcoming and professional reception; a special appreciation for the medical director, Dr. Marco Maggi, who is caring for our cat; my only regret: having only recently encountered the San Francesco Hospital.

I came here for an emergency with a kitten who was just a few months old. They responded promptly, providing all the necessary assistance and also kindly answering all my questions. I don't often leave reviews, but this time I really appreciated their professionalism and I thank them ❤️

I'm giving one star only because it's the only thing I can give less. I'd read positive comments, but perhaps it was because of the visits. We needed help for our furry friend: we showed up at the emergency room at 7 in the morning, received an initial check-up, and were asked to wait. After an hour and a half, still nothing, and whenever we ask, we're always told we have to wait. We went to another clinic where they saw him right away: acute renal failure requiring immediate surgery and hospitalization. It's a good thing there are other clinics, because it's better to lose an emergency room like this than to find one. If it hadn't been an emergency, I would have made an appointment. You must have had other emergencies, but if you know you can't, send me away; don't leave me standing there waiting for who knows how long.
Dr. Rossi from the emergency room: very competent, honest in explaining all the pros and cons, and very empathetic. Thank you, Doc!

I've been calling every day for a week and after 10 minutes of waiting in the call queue, they kick me out..... I also contacted you by email and I've been waiting for your response for days.... What service do you provide????
Always kind and sweet with our furry friends, competent and well-prepared, it's always a guarantee. A special thanks to Dr. Rachele Huobet who took care of my Kimba 🐶. …

They must be excellent doctors. It's a shame I've been waiting three weeks for a call for a biopsy and the phone is silent. After four days, I called to postpone the appointment and still nothing. In the end, I opted for another clinic. Dear Sirs, if an owner calls you to schedule a biopsy, they don't do it lightly. It would be good manners to answer. Never again.

Edit: I'm currently in Zurich for radiotherapy, so I can't call. Anyway, my last name is Castelnuovo, and I called on February 11th and 13th. The only thing I'd point out, and I'll stop here, is that these complaints haven't been so uncommon for some time. Perhaps, rather than understanding, it would be necessary to intervene. Regards.

PS: Unfortunately, I've fallen for it again. I arrived at 9 am for an emergency and left to go to Malpensa (Anicura) to receive treatment. Well done.
Well-equipped facility and Dr. Luperto are SUPER: kind, competent, empathetic, and patient! Thank you!

I've been to the clinic a few times with my cat and I'd like to thank all the staff, including the receptionists, for their patience, kindness, and friendliness. I understand that it's not easy to manage a clinic with a constant flow of patients and phone calls. The doctors who treated my cat Briosce were very attentive, friendly, and professional. I find the clinic's prices fair, very honest compared to other facilities. I highly recommend it, thank you!

This afternoon we went to the emergency room for a nosebleed and we were given a quote of €850.00, a SHAME, we refused and went to another facility where they asked us for €300.00, on May 1st, a holiday and at night they asked us for €500.00. A year ago for a kitten found on the street they asked us for €1600.00, we are truly out of our minds, they are no longer vets it is just a question of making money and speculating on our animals. I will never set foot in there again, if I could put it below zero I would.
As for veterinary intervention, nothing to say, but the management of invoices and payments needs to be reviewed.

We wanted to thank Dr. Paolo Viola for his humanity, availability, and professionalism, for accompanying our Zeus across the Rainbow Bridge.
Recognizing such a difficult time, he managed to make everything easier, thanks to his empathy.
We thank all the staff.

Unfortunately, this facility doesn't deserve any stars. It should also change its name, as it's an insult to Saint Francis. It should also remove the wording "24/7," which isn't true, and the response "there's no shift worker, it can happen" after checking in and triaging is absolutely unjustifiable. We arrived at the facility on Tuesday, April 28th, just before 7:00 PM, with a Newfoundland dog in critical condition, dejected and having serious difficulty walking. After the initial triage assessment, a temperature of 41.5°C was noted, and we were assured that even with the emergency room full, she would be examined because her condition was not good. We waited, and after about twenty minutes, the doctor arrived, and with no regard for the people present, she would have been better off hiding in a small room to express her total indifference, declaring that her shift was over and that she absolutely would not be examining "this dog," before turning her back and going to examine another dog that was already there. The doctor never addressed us, who were standing there half a meter away with the dog lying in front of the reception desk; she always addressed only the staff, leaving the hot potato to her colleague. The situation was so surreal that I didn't realize it was us. The colleague present, the receptionist, and the nurse who had performed triage repeatedly asked her, "Are you sure? It's a green code?"
After that, we were told that since there was no shift worker, and this is something that can happen, we would have to go elsewhere and that we should have made a phone call first...of course, in an emergency, you look for the nearest clinic and rely on the EMERGENCY ROOM 24/7 wording, and you rush to the scene for a suspected gastric torsion. In defiance of Aristotle's oath, we were quickly dismissed without even receiving any help to get poor Tara back on her feet, and without even holding the door open for us...help came from another person who was there with their dog...speechless, and please specify on your website that emergency room is not guaranteed.

A truly professional, clean, and welcoming clinic for both us, the owners, and our furry friends. A special thank you from the receptionists to the doctors, and especially to Dr. Maggi, who is not only a competent doctor but also a person with values. Highly recommended!

Thank you so much, Mr. Romualdo! We're happy you had a positive experience at our hospital. Our team is committed to providing high-quality veterinary services, and your feedback is a great motivation for us. Best regards, from the entire team.

I think being a veterinarian means treating animals in any situation.
Last night, our dog wasn't well and had a truly disastrous clinical picture.
We entered this clinic and they let us in without the dog being examined. After an hour of waiting, a dog with some diarrhea arrived and was taken and examined. After the vet left, we asked for an explanation and she told us that our dog was code green and that we should wait in case other emergencies arose, so we got up and left.
This morning, the dog was admitted to another facility with a life-threatening situation if we waited another day.
If you're a veterinarian, don't do it for the money; do it because you love animals; otherwise, it's better to change careers.
I'll answer here: it's clear you don't have an archive; no admissions were made or delivered; otherwise, it wouldn't have ended with a simple review.
Good, professional and attentive

Good afternoon, Ms. Brbagallo,
we're sorry to hear that your experience wasn't satisfactory.

At this time, however, we don't have any data in our system that can be linked to your report, and we're therefore unable to trace the incident you're referring to.

If you'd like to learn more about what happened, we invite you to contact us directly so we can verify the situation in detail and provide you with a timely response.

We remain at your disposal.
San Francesco Veterinary Hospital

Terrible incompetents!! I take my dog ​​in at night because he was swollen and had various problems... with tests in hand, a man without any skill or art because calling him a doctor would be blasphemy, he doesn't even look at the dog, he doesn't look at the tests and parks us in the waiting room... after 2 hours of waiting, a pseudo doctor comes out and lets in a dog with diarrhea while my dog ​​was dying!! I got angry and she told me it was a green code!!! Incompetent!!!!! Now he is in a serious condition hospitalized in another clinic that is MUCH MORE COMPETENT! Ah, they didn't even check him in!! Never again!!!

If I could put a 0, I would. At their clinic, the dog was a green code and could have waited all night in the waiting room (they didn't even read the blood tests, which showed a red code clinical picture). At another clinic, they admitted him the same morning because his life was at risk. You are SHAMEFUL! Change your profession!!!! Especially those of you who worked the shift between the night of April 17, 2026 and April 18, 2026, are INCOMPETENT. Reportable.
My 13-year-old Dachshund with heart disease has been treated by Dr. Ilaria Spada for about a year and I feel great, she's a wonderful and very knowledgeable person.
Professionalism and courtesy. Three hours of waiting without a reservation was worth the service. Congratulations. And it's not the first time 👍 …

I arrived at the San Francesco clinic at night after being turned down (over the phone) by another clinic closer to my home. The doctor, whose name I don't even know, immediately took Matteo the cat in and examined him. The situation was very serious. In the end, I discovered a caring and loving doctor, as well as an honest and helpful clinic. Matteo, from heaven, and I thank you for everything.

ANNOYING AND RUDE STAFF. A REAL DISGRACE. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOSPITAL TO ANYONE.

PLUS, YOU'LL PAY FOUR TIMES IF THEY TAKE ADVANTAGE OF YOU!!!!
I would like to commend Mrs. VALENTINA at reception for her kind availability, courtesy, and professionalism.
Very good and kind. They saved my dog. A heartfelt thank you to the intensive care unit and internal medicine.
Skilled, empathetic, and competent, they truly demonstrate what it means to love your job! Highly recommended clinic.

They saw my Dorothy right away, and were very kind.
Unfortunately, the diagnosis was dire.
They didn't charge us anything for the visit.
Truly excellent treatment.
Super kind doctor. Highly recommended.
Very friendly staff who were able to handle a late night emergency.

My dog ​​had a walking problem. Everything went well with the first few visits, but then, due to a real need, I emailed the doctor for support, but I never received a response.
Beyond ethics, this doctor lacks sensitivity, integrity, and, above all, good manners.
I'm not mentioning the orthopedic neurologist only because I'm more polite than him.
This clinic is strongly discouraged based on my personal experience.

We're very sorry to hear about your negative experience at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital. We invite you to contact us directly to discuss the situation and find a solution. Thank you for sharing your feedback. Sincerely, San Francesco Veterinary Hospital

It's funny to receive this standardized response here publicly, inviting me to contact you to clarify what happened, but to receive no response to the email I sent you a week ago, even before reviewing the property here.

Dear Marco, we're sorry to hear that your experience at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital was unsatisfactory. We couldn't find your name on the records, so we couldn't contact you. We invite you to contact us directly to discuss your situation and find a solution.
Best regards,
San Francesco Veterinary Hospital

Dear Alessio, we're very sorry to hear about your negative experience at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital. We invite you to contact us directly to discuss the situation and find a solution. Thank you for your feedback; it will help us improve our services. San Francesco Veterinary Hospital

This evening I had a truly positive experience with Dr. Fabrizio Biagini.
He dedicated so much time to the visit, without rushing me, sitting down with me and carefully listening to all my concerns.

We evaluated the most appropriate treatment together, clearly explaining each step and answering all my questions. I felt welcomed, understood, and truly supported in my needs.

It's rare to meet such attentive, compassionate, and helpful professionals. He's not just a great veterinarian: he's a special person.

I highly recommend him to everyone.

Dr. Ferriani and Dr. Boiocchi are extraordinary doctors who never stopped searching until they found the right solution for our dog. They are highly regarded experts in their field, with a deep understanding of the latest scientific literature, and they continue to continuously educate themselves on our dog's specific situation.

If you have a complex case where other veterinarians give up, they are the right professionals to turn to. We couldn't be more grateful to have such competent and determined specialists at our side, who do everything they can, even when the case is particularly challenging.

Thank you so much, Alice, for your positive review! We're happy to hear you had a positive experience at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital. Our mission is to provide the best possible service to our patients. Best regards, from the San Francesco Veterinary Hospital team 🥰 …

Thank you so much, Vanessa! We're so happy you had such a positive experience with us. Your support is greatly appreciated and motivates us to always do better. Best regards, from the team at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital 🥰 …
Excellent clinic with human and prepared people. My experience with Dr. Liliana Carnevale was more than excellent, good and professional.

A truly beautiful, well-maintained, and welcoming facility with separate waiting rooms for cats and dogs. They have cat carriers available to keep cats from becoming unnerved. The approach was very professional and genuinely concerned about my little cat's health. We were very satisfied with Dr. Maggi, who was clear in his explanations and instructions. They even saw us without an appointment. Overall, we are very satisfied.

Today, with great sadness and regret, a chapter closes in this, my beloved veterinary clinic, not only for the extraordinary expertise of its veterinarians but also for its ethical approach and strong focus on animal welfare. But today, a key person is leaving us: for the first impression, for the smooth running of the reception, for the ability to understand priorities at a glance, all while answering a thousand calls simultaneously, managing arrivals and registrations, couriers, etc. A person who three people would not be able to replace is leaving us: not a doctor, not a veterinary technician, but an extremely efficient and organized woman, with an innate ability to solve problems and understand emergencies. Barbara Baratti was and will remain, in the memory of ALL her clients, an irreplaceable cornerstone of what this wonderful veterinary clinic was before her acquisition. The maximum star rating is obviously for Barbara, not for the management. Good luck, Barbara, after the downturn... 💔

I was saddened to learn of Ms. Barbara Baratti's resignation, and I would like to extend my sincere appreciation.
The efficiency of a facility is also evident in the people who work at the Front Office. I have had the opportunity several times, while waiting to be seen by a veterinarian, to witness Ms. Baratti's professionalism, courtesy, and above all, her expertise in carrying out her duties, answering a constant stream of phone calls, simultaneously managing the reception desk and the various incoming couriers (there may have been other duties, but these are the cases I have personally witnessed). I believe it will be difficult to find another person with the same qualities to replace her.
I wish Ms. Baratti the best and the best of luck in her future career.

Dear Carlo Francesco Anelli, thank you for your valuable feedback and positive rating! We're delighted you had a great experience at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital. Our team is committed to providing high-quality services, and we're happy this was reflected in your stay. We look forward to welcoming you back!

We rushed to this emergency room because my dog ​​was very ill and it was a matter of time. We arrived and I immediately explained my dog's symptoms: a swollen belly, difficulty doing his business, crying and staggering. The doctor admitted that it could be gastric torsion, which is very serious if not treated in time. What they told us was "you have to go to the San Siro Clinic on Via Gallarate." Now, I don't remember exactly why my poor dog couldn't be admitted there, and unfortunately, at the end of all this, he died that same morning. It doesn't seem right to me, especially if it's an emergency room; it should be suitable for any type of emergency and not send potentially serious patients to other facilities. Otherwise, why are you even open to being an emergency room? It's certainly not the main reason for the death, but the staff and organization are definitely terrible.

Thank you so much for your review, Cinzia! We're happy to hear you had a positive experience. Our goal is always to provide excellent service, and we're happy you appreciated it. Best regards from the entire hospital team!

I arrived at the facility around 4:00 PM, after my dog ​​had suffered severe, closely spaced seizures. She had been sedated by our veterinarian, who had referred us there for further evaluation, given her extremely critical clinical situation.
I understand that, under certain circumstances, an emergency room may be forced to divert certain patients. However, I find it unacceptable that a 24-hour emergency veterinary clinic would not admit a comatose dog with ongoing seizures. Regardless, the receptionists' behavior was grossly irresponsible. I was told to go to "the other location at Via Lampugnano 8, five minutes from here." Neither of them bothered to verify the address or the actual distance. I was directed to a facility that was not an active clinic for that type of emergency, and was also closed and dedicated to large animals. This mistake forced me to waste even more precious time: after realizing my mistake, I had to drive further to finally find the correct clinic, accumulating a total delay of over 25 minutes. All this while I had a dog in the car in very serious condition, on the verge of death.
I know this report will likely be viewed superficially, perhaps even with a certain irony, and that it is unlikely to have any concrete consequences. But know that in those minutes lost due to incorrect information, I had a dog dying in the car. A dog that actually died at the clinic I managed to reach. The outcome probably wouldn't have changed even if you had taken her in, but that in no way justifies such a superficial handling of an emergency situation. Anyone who works in an emergency room, even at the front desk, must be fully aware of the context in which they operate.
I seriously urge you to reflect on the adequacy, training, and responsibility of the reception staff, because what happened is incompatible with an emergency service.

The best in Milan. If our dog is still here with us, we owe it to them. Our French bulldog Matilda underwent emergency surgery for internal bleeding on January 1st and was hospitalized for a week. We were cared for by a team of very young but highly trained professionals, and I can only thank them for what they did. A special thanks to Drs. Coden, Huober, Fumagalli, and Dr. Costa.

I've only been to this clinic once and I'll never go back.
I brought my dog, a boxer, who unfortunately had a wound that had been stitched up six days earlier (surgery they didn't perform).
I arrived at 9:15 PM and the dog had an opening of about 2 cm. They did what they called triage without even looking at the dog.
There were two other patients in the room with what they said were serious cases (but I don't doubt that).
After three hours, so at midnight, they told me that the wait had been extended and that they could give me other directions.
Meanwhile, the wound had opened completely, and the dog, a 46 kg boxer, had become unmanageable due to the pain.
I called and asked them to at least look at him, and they told me he had a green code with a hole in his back and was full of blood.
They saw him at 2:00 a.m. and told me they could only put a bandage on him, treat him, and then take him to the surgery location because they don't have a surgeon, but they sent him the video and he or she could make a diagnosis from the comfort of their home!
We waited 5 hours, paid €180 for them to put a bandage on the dog, arrived there with a small opening, and after 5 hours the
dog was completely open.
I'm truly shocked.
You can't call yourself an emergency room, be obviously understaffed, and then tell yourself after 3 hours to go somewhere else.
I honestly strongly advise against this place, at least for emergencies.
I absolutely recommend the clinic, I always bring my dogs and Dr. Pratesi is number one

I wasn't personally familiar with this clinic. My vet recommended it to me. I brought my dog ​​Pollux there on December 28th because he wasn't feeling well. They admitted him and operated on him the next day for intestinal obstruction. The staff was incredibly competent, helpful, and loving with animals and people. They kept us updated daily, both by phone and in person, on our dog's condition. He was discharged yesterday, and today I went back to the clinic, worried about the dirty bandage. Even though they'd given me all the instructions when I was discharged, they reassured me and promptly changed the bandage, even giving me what I needed for the next change. I highly recommend this clinic!
I called for an emergency appointment, and the lady who answered was extremely annoyed and even snorted. She hung up on me very rudely. I'll go elsewhere.

Dear Pamy,

We're very sorry to hear that your experience wasn't satisfactory. We appreciate your feedback and are committed to improving. We invite you to contact us directly to discuss the situation and find a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and hope to offer you a better experience in the future. Thank you for writing to us.

Dear Elisabetta,

We sincerely thank you for your positive review. We're happy to hear you had a great experience with us. 🥰

Best regards

San Francesco Veterinary Hospital

I wanted to thank Dr. Martina Zarotti for taking care of our dog Jack last night. She was very good at explaining everything to us in detail. 🫶 Being the only vet there, I saw her running around patiently to assist each case. She was very kind and excellent. Our Jack is doing great. Thank you so much ❤️ …

I arrived at 7:30 PM with my cat, who had just been diagnosed by the vet with severe anemia and difficulty breathing, along with abdominal effusion, which was diagnosed by x-ray. An ultrasound was performed at the hospital, revealing nodules on the peritoneum and internal bleeding. To determine exactly what was wrong, I was advised to have a CT scan, costing €3,500. At that point, since I'm not wealthy, I had no choice but to let my cat go. Furthermore, before I even got on the phone with the receptionist, who didn't know the cat's condition, I was told that if the cat needed to be admitted overnight, it would cost me €2,000. It seems to me like speculation on animal health. I hope these prices aren't in line with other veterinary hospitals in Milan. Unfortunately, in an emergency, San Francesco was the first to offer me an ultrasound.

It was a Friday afternoon and my dog ​​suddenly felt ill, and we took him to the clinic. The doctors rushed over immediately because the lady at reception understood the emergency. In fact, it was a bedsore. They informed us of a cardiac tamponade and that they were working on it. So far, so good; the team seems attentive and sensitive, and they perform a pericardial tamponade. A shift change and the doctor takes over, discussing the emergency room; the previous colleague confirms that they will perform a test on the fluid collected to determine the extent of the problem and the cause of the effusion. Our little dog had been suffering from a heart murmur, so he had been tired for a while, even though he was under observation. We notified him of this.
The emergency room "doctor" welcomes us into the office, and we waste about half an hour speculating, but nothing is clear. Then he turns to customer service, offering a quote for multiple nights, which we needed to approve before treating the dog. At that moment, I would have given blood just to get immediate action. I didn't care about the amount of the estimate, it's not a sweater or a house... Finally, after paying the deposit, he told us he'd be seen by the cardiologist and the echocardiogram would tell us the extent of the problem. They would contact us the next day... They hadn't been able to do anything with the recovered fluid. So they would have recovered the sample in case a second swab test was necessary.
The next day, no one contacted us, and we went in mid-day to find out...
A "doctor" greeted us and explained that there was a suspicion of something serious and that she was waiting for the echocardiogram results... Meanwhile, she warned us that we might lose him, partly because they were convinced there was a mass but that it would be difficult to diagnose.
We spoke with the cardiologist, who introduced herself and confirmed there could be a mass that offered no hope but could only be diagnosed by an echocardiogram. I asked if it could be related to a hemorrhage from a heart attack that had resulted in a hemorrhage clustering in the pericardium, since he had been tired for a few months after the apparent heart murmur. She replied that she couldn't confirm this directly, but that for her it was a mass that was making the situation dire. Even with surgery, recovery would have been difficult, and even taking him home that day wouldn't have guaranteed her survival. But she couldn't guarantee it, since there was no proof. Meanwhile, the fluid from the second tamponade performed midday hadn't been analyzed. Therefore, her hypotheses were based only on the general outline of the cardiac ultrasound.
So the only thing left to do was say goodbye. We asked to be able to stay with him but to leave when they took action. They confirmed that this was absolutely the case. My colleague began administering the substance to put him to sleep in our presence, but realized the amount wasn't enough, and while I was telling him I was about to leave so as not to witness it any further, she confirmed that he was already gone... It tore my heart apart, and I couldn't understand anything at that moment. As if, since the anesthesia wasn't enough, she had immediately injected the final injection while he was still awake. I've been incapable of peace since that moment; I still haven't understood why she acted that way, what my little one had done wrong to suffer so much until the end, and what I had done wrong to witness such suffering. It was Saturday... All I have left of him are his ashes...after 14 years...
I don't wish anyone to suffer as we are still suffering, even because of how events unfolded...Now we're trying to retrace and reflect on how things unfolded, and now I'm terrified of getting a new puppy in the future because I wouldn't know who to turn to if he needed medical attention, given his terrible experience.

Professionalism, expertise, and availability.
Very affectionate with my cat.
A heartfelt thank you to the Cardiology Department, especially Dr. Ilaria Spalla, a team of truly wonderful doctors, both professionally and personally. THANK YOU!

A huge thank you to veterinarians Sara Bazzo and Vincenza Caporale! They are incredibly professional, friendly, and dog-loving doctors! They helped my puppy with her patellar luxation, allowing her to walk normally again! And a huge thank you to receptionist Eleonora for her patience and kindness!

I went to the San Francesco hospital during the night because my 3-month-old dog was sick. As soon as we arrived, Dr. Messina welcomed us and, with her professionalism, competence, and ability, she immediately understood that it was parvovirus. Our puppy's condition immediately appeared serious, so he needed to be admitted to intensive care. The hospital stay lasted a good 3 weeks, but in the end, they saved him. 3 weeks where I was contacted by phone up to 3 times a day. Support from all the intensive care staff. All the doctors who treated my little "LORD" were attentive, scrupulous, professional, and always available. I must thank them all, without exception, for the work they did. They all contributed to his recovery. The care and support offered by the San Francesco clinic is excellent. Thank you. Thank you from little LORD. Nothing to say about professionalism but for some time I have noticed a notable increase in the costs of both visits and therapies. For example, you cannot spend €80 to remove a seed from your eye, the visit lasting less than a quarter of an hour.
Good evening, I'm extremely satisfied with the service and the speed with which my cat was examined. Thank you, you are exemplary professionals!
Maximum availability and professionalism. Thank you.
I highly recommend this veterinary clinic for the competence, professionalism, and kindness of the staff.
A thank you from the entire team at San Francesco Veterinary Hospital for the five-star rating. The Management

excellent service, perfect hygiene, super service

Over the past few months, I've often had to seek medical care from the doctors at this hospital for my cat Gonzalo. Molly is now home safe and sound, one eye less, but surrounded by all the love she deserves.

Dear Giacinto, thank you for your kind review and the time you took to share it with us. We are always proud to be able to convey our passion and commitment to caring for our pets.
We wish you a wonderful day. San Francesco Veterinary Hospital

Unfortunately, my experience wasn't positive.
Yesterday afternoon, I urgently needed to contact the clinic, but after several phone calls, I was unable to get through.
I think it's a serious problem that a veterinary clinic doesn't guarantee even a minimal level of availability, because at certain times, it can really make a difference to the animals' health.
I'm giving it two stars only because many people have spoken highly of it, but unfortunately, I haven't had the opportunity to verify this in person.

I would have given this excellent veterinary practice five stars. Unfortunately, the poor afternoon management of the receptionists and switchboard greatly detracts from the overall service. If you have an emergency, it's literally impossible to contact them in the afternoon, while in the morning the same service is impeccable, fast, and thorough. I hope they improve the afternoon service...

Good morning,

I'd like to start by saying that I've known the San Francesco Clinic for many years. I took my dog, who was seriously ill with epilepsy, there for years, and I can only say that they were the best, as they still are.
My review concerns the receptionist. For some time now, the wait for a response in the afternoon has been endless. The person managing the afternoon receptionist doesn't answer, and I often have to call back multiple times. It seems almost impossible to schedule an appointment or get a response for any issue, and when you do, they're disorganized.
In the morning, the problem doesn't persist. The receptionist, who is always answered by Ms. Barbara, is always prompt. I've always managed to get appointments and responses promptly.
Having known the facility for many years, I believe they should continue to have competent and qualified staff even in the afternoon, because in an emergency, you risk not receiving the right treatment.
I'm a loyal customer, and as such, I took the liberty of writing this review.
Have a good day.

Good morning, I was there with my wife on Saturday and I can only say thank you to the San Francesco Clinic and especially to Barbara's wonderful, professional, and reassuring welcome at the reception. Sometimes a smile is worth more than a thousand words! ❤️

I had to go to this facility for an orthopedic appointment, and I was assisted by Dr. Sara Bazzo. Professionalism, efficiency, empathy, and ongoing updates. I highly recommend this clinic. My little pets have been treated at this facility since 2016. I'd like to thank Dr. Boselli, who saved my little Biba's life and has cared for her with love and empathy ever since. Dr. Bottero, who treated my beloved Michelle, ensuring she no longer suffered from gastrointestinal issues day in and day out. I went to the emergency room with my cat who was very ill. After an hour of waiting, and after the people who came after me had already entered, I was still there waiting.

Terrible Experience – Dangerous Facility and Unacceptable Clinical Management

My cat was admitted to this clinic in mid-July 2025, and what happened was not only disappointing, but seriously dangerous to his health.

The medical staff who handled the case—both night and day—proved inexperienced, unprepared, and completely incapable of making a correct diagnosis, even explicitly admitting uncertainty about the procedures to be performed.

The cause of my cat's discomfort was a severe sore throat, easily identified with a simple oral examination. Instead, he was subjected to unnecessary tests, kept in a cage in questionable hygienic conditions, and treatments (such as a nasogastric tube) that could have been fatal were proposed.

Furthermore, we were given a completely incorrect diagnosis of "gastroenteritis," without any compatible symptoms.

In light of all this, a €1,600 estimate was presented, demonstrating that financial considerations seem to outweigh the animals' well-being.

My detailed complaint was to no avail: the clinic denied any responsibility, hiding behind a generic "we followed the protocol," without taking any responsibility for the clinical negligence demonstrated.

I strongly advise against this facility. Entrusting an animal to them can pose a serious risk to its life.

I am taking legal action because people have a right to know and animals have a right to be treated professionally and conscientiously.

The reception staff is completely incompetent and arrogant. They don't listen to you at all: I waited 45 minutes while they kept calling other people. When I left, they didn't even apologize or bother to answer. Terrible place.

I want to thank Dr. Andrea Rossi of the Emergency Department, who cared for a colony cat with expertise, common sense, and great empathy.

Dr. (???) Erica Civitillo is completely incompetent, arrogant, and makes incorrect diagnoses without performing tests. If you love your pets, don't trust this..."professional"...

I don't know if after this experience I'll ever have the strength to adopt a new pet, but I know for sure who I should turn to if I do.

Good morning, I took my little Peggy to the emergency room. Dr. Barbara took great care and dedication to her little girl, with very kindness. Unfortunately, her medical condition was very serious, and she passed away a few days later.

My dog ​​Nancy was saved by Dr. Pratesi.

I wouldn't even give it one star. I had a terrible experience with my dog. He was choking. In a panic, I immediately called this number. I tried to ask what I could do at that moment, because it was only a matter of seconds. I was desperately trying to ask during the call how to perform first aid. All they could do was tell me to take him to the clinic (in time to get in the car, the dog would have died). Furthermore, after my numerous requests to do something to save him, they ended up hanging up on me. Shame on you.
I'll never come again. I waited three hours for an appointment and went home without any resolution. The time for a single appointment is about two hours, unacceptable.

A huge thank you to all the staff at the San Francesco clinic. On Saturday evening, they performed a true miracle when they managed to save our beloved dog Russel, with such professionalism and a huge dose of love.
During holidays and at night, there are long waits and staff are understaffed. Furthermore, they don't provide physical copies of x-rays. Strongly discouraged.

Good morning to everyone reading and responding. I'd like to point out that my review isn't intended to spark controversy, but rather to clarify what happened. I brought my 8-year-old German Shepherd, Sony, to you on Wednesday morning for an ultrasound. The dog, who has always suffered from cystitis and stones, had been experiencing additional symptoms in recent weeks, including lameness, loss of appetite, and weight loss. I suspect prostate cancer, given his difficulty defecating. Numerous tests were performed, including blood gases and an X-ray, costing €800 under sedation, not in an emergency room setting. To my surprise, the tests were all negative; the dog was "fine" (the sonographer said), but they also arbitrarily performed a urine sample via cystocentesis (with a 2.57 cm stone in his bladder, I wouldn't have done it...). When it came time to pay, the cost had risen to €800... I asked for clarification, but whatever... the important thing was that the dog was "well"... he was also diagnosed with only balanitis, which needed antibiotics. I got home and in the late afternoon, Sony developed a urinary blockage. I waited until midnight, hoping the dog would "unblock" himself. It all seemed surreal, considering I'd been to your clinic a few hours earlier and the dog was urinating perfectly! On the phone, a kind doctor told me she would try catheterizing him but couldn't admit him due to lack of space. I answered, and I almost reassured her, "Doctor, one thing at a time," convinced and confident that it wasn't that serious. I arrived at 1:00 a.m., and seeing the dog with his glans, now triple its size and exposed by the foreskin (I repeat, it wasn't like this in the morning), I suspected a tumor (yes, but what if the ultrasound, X-ray, and tests were all negative?). I opted for euthanasia because Sony was suffering from being euthanized on the floor. That's how my Sony died, and I still don't understand what happened. I've consulted with other colleagues, and they all agree that whoever performed the cystocentesis inadvertently ruptured the bladder stone (it was too large to pass through the urethra and had been in Sony's bladder for some time). It's likely true that there was a hidden tumor, but what a terrible experience for wanting to investigate further. I'll leave aside the money issue, which is suicide to pay €800 for four tests. I'll also leave aside the fact that I'm still waiting for someone to call me to get my Sony's ashes back (I opted for a single cremation), even though I understand that's not your responsibility. I called and was coldly told, "They took him away a little while ago, they'll probably call you on Monday." A little empathy, my esteemed Medical Director, a little more pathos in the truest sense of the word. Sony's fate was certainly sealed. If there were mistakes, however, that's a more serious matter. But neither you nor I will ever know. I only know that, unfortunately, I can't recommend your hospital. At least for routine tests, you may be good, but a cystocentesis should be done by someone with experience, not someone who needs experience, especially not on a dog that's no longer young and has a stone the size of a house. The doubt remains. I want to convince myself that Sony had a terrible disease and that now she's finally stopped suffering, but it's a belief that helps me move on, not a medical diagnosis, which is what I was looking for from you or what I would have preferred to have been given. It's all very, very sad.

As always, the doctors at Clinica San Francesco stand out for their professionalism and dedication. My dog ​​will always be cared for only by them: an extraordinary team, kind, caring, loving, and patient. I can't thank you enough for everything you do!

I should also add that since my dog ​​is a total mischief maker, I'd better ask for an honorary membership card!

My daughter, Freccia, had surgery a week ago.
I thank Dr. Bazzo for all her support.
I highly recommend this clinic.

It's my go-to clinic for both general and specialist visits (Sartori, the dermatologist, is excellent). Carlo at the reception desk is also fantastic, always courteous and helpful, even when I had to speak to him on the phone about an emergency. Thank you so much :)

Veterinary clinic with sky-high costs. I went in August with my Dalmatian who wasn't well. They treated him for neurological problems, ignoring the breed-specific issue with kidney stones. He was discharged after a week with the recommendation of physiotherapy. The dog then stopped eating, and the clinic recommended giving him pills to boost his appetite. He still didn't eat, so we brought him back to the clinic on August 28th, and he died at midnight. They told us he had a bacterial infection that probably started from the catheter and reached the heart. Simba is no longer with us, and all of this is due to the incompetence of the staff present in August. They were all interns with no experience. I say this because I went every day and never saw anyone over 30 with experience with breeds. I'll close by saying that if you charge like sky-high prices, YOU CAN'T MAKE ERRORS. This clinic should be closed. If you search for my name, don't say you can't find anything; it's not possible. Maybe that's what suits you best. Everyone remembers the dog there at the clinic. He was a Dalmatian who didn't go unnoticed given the type of dog he was. Semi wants to contact me, as he says. He can find me on Facebook with photos of Simba. Antonello Pezzetta

I highly recommend this clinic... all the doctors are excellent, Barbara is always efficient and kind. The only flaw this evening: arrogance!
In a very difficult moment, I called and the lady, in a very arrogant tone, told me she didn't have time to handle my emergency. Beautiful clinic, well-trained doctors, they should just learn to answer the phone more politely, and when you ask for a call back, they should do so because it's polite, especially considering it's not free.
We waited two hours for an appointment only to be told the doctor we were looking for had an emergency, too bad no one bothered to tell us.

They've been caring for my Great Dane with care and attention for years. Less than a year ago, on a Saturday night, they didn't hesitate to perform emergency surgery, saving her life. A special thanks also goes to Carlo and Elisa, who are always available and kind.

If Barbara greets you at the front desk, you're in excellent hands. Knowledgeable, kind, and empathetic, she goes out of her way to help every owner in the waiting room. Excellent doctors. Ever since they saved my dog ​​with a terrible diagnosis, they've become my go-to clinic for all my pets.

I want to thank Dr. Laura Della Tomba for her professionalism, competence, and empathy when putting my sick cat to sleep. She was there for me during the decision and afterward. And Dr. Luperto, who cared for me during my illness. She was incredibly human and competent. Thank you.

Welcoming and clean place
Qualified, competent, and kind medical and paramedical staff.
They handled my dog's emergency with great professionalism.
Swallowing a needle is incredibly rare, but the medical team performed a miracle!
Thank you

Judging by the number of young patients who come to this hospital, it seems to be working well. The worried faces on our faces—I like to call ourselves guardians, not owners of our pets—say a lot about how much love we have for our pets, who are full members of our families. My cat is being treated by the ophthalmologist Dr. De Stefanis for a serious eye problem. What can I say? Seven years ago, the doctor saved my cat's eye from a nasty case of herpes. A few months ago, the same eye, another problem: a perforated corneal ulcer. Surgery was performed at another clinic, but the post-op wasn't going well. After a while, I managed to have my first appointment with Dr. De Stefanis, changed therapy, and since then, the eye has progressively improved, so much so that I'm no longer worried about it needing another operation. My cat and I found in the doctor: above all, great professionalism and experience, but also sensitivity and attention to the pet, and extreme care in explaining the pathology's progress. A huge thank you from me and my pet.
I'm adding before and after photos of 5 months of therapy, now almost complete. Maintenance therapy is just now underway. December 3, 2024

An infinite thank you

We want to sincerely thank Elena for the excellent care we received. The doctor was professional, competent, and very kind. She explained everything calmly and reassured us about our puppy. The staff was prompt, helpful, and truly attentive to everyone. We can only recommend this hospital!

Congratulations to Dr. Claudia Marzorati for her efficiency and expertise, without unnecessary frills.
You don't know it, but what was perhaps "routine" for us could have been such a tragedy that it would have torn families apart... it saved our lives.
A very clever puppy (just under 3 months old) decided to swallow a sock.
He couldn't get out from behind, and we had a tight deadline to get him out from the front, with the risk of him falling further and further down, with obvious consequences (the thought of having to operate on a puppy terrified us).
She let us in without wasting time on unnecessary pleasantries, straight to the point: after a minute she had administered the injection, after another minute the dog was vomiting the blessed sock, and after another minute she had already injected the antagonist to stop him from vomiting.
I've had dogs for over 15 years; I've seen some truly brilliant veterinarians. I love pragmatism, problem-solvers who know how to do it competently (even just with an injection, I've seen it all).
€90 well spent. Yes, nighttime clinics cost more. It's true, they make a lot of money out of it, and many are oriented toward that (I've had experience, I repeat, in almost all of Milan's nighttime clinics, despite myself).
For the benefit of those who read this, I'll write the following:
In an emergency, we called
- Gran Sasso Clinic: they told us to go there, get a general exam and X-ray, and to come back the next day for another X-ray to see what the situation was (you might be wondering, why an X-ray? To confirm that there's a sock after I told you I saw him swallow it? Yes, someone is making money out of this...
- MypetClinic Clinic: at least the doctor was honest, saying that since he was a puppy, and an endoscopy was likely, she didn't feel like it.
- Tibaldi Clinic: given the three-hour wait, she recommended San Francesco Clinic.

The day after her first vaccination, a 2-month-old puppy was brought in, her condition unclear even before the visit: she definitely has a neurological problem. After the visit and various tests, it's clear she doesn't have a neurological problem. Hospitalization for observation is recommended. The next day, the little girl feels better, but hospitalization is recommended again to facilitate her recovery. The next day, she sees another doctor, and she definitely has a neurological problem. She isn't eating, and according to the doctor, she needs to be tube-fed. Unfortunately, I can't attach the three videos taken at the clinic of the puppy eating without problems from the owner's hand. Brought home, against their advice, she immediately started playing with her mother and aunt and ate without problems. I have many questions, but I'll leave it up to those who read this review to make their own assessments, and I recommend reading other reviews as well. Unfortunately, in addition to not letting me publish the video, I'm forced to give it one star.
